title: Probabilistic trace gating and hot-path minimal sampler
creator: Asha Khatri
description:
Background: production tracing at Redwood currently adds measurable CPU and allocation pressure on hot request paths (in particular gateway + inference edge). Recent prod incidents show spikes in tracer CPU during bursts; existing tail-based and reservoir samplers reduce emitted traces but still require decision logic on the hot path that increases p50 service CPU and allocs.

Goal: implement a lightweight probabilistic 'trace gate' at ingress that makes an approximate, constant-time decision with minimal allocations. Full, heavyweight sampling (tail evaluation, span encoding, KV cache capture) will be performed only for requests that pass the gate. This should reduce hot-path overhead by >=40% while keeping tail trace capture (p99 trace availability for latency regressions) within current bounds.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Hot-path tracer CPU usage reduction >=40% on high-QPS services (measured by eBPF / instance profiles).
- Additional per-request latency overhead <=0.2ms median and <=1.0ms p99 attributable to the gate.
- Traces emitted per-minute reduced by >=30% while p99 latency anomaly detection F1 score degrades by <5%.

Design proposal:
1) Lightweight gate at the ingress (implemented in the proxy layer): compute an approximate score using a tiny feature set (request latency sketch hint, route weight, customer tier, random hash). Use DDSketch/quantile summary and a small, preallocated RNG state to decide probabilistically. Gate path must not allocate and must avoid locks.
2) For positive gates, attach a short token and enqueue for 'rich sampling' handled by a background worker pool in the runtime that does full span capture, tail heuristics, and encoding. Worker pool admits bounded concurrency to cap memory.
3) Negative gates still allow rare reservoir samples (global low-rate accept) to preserve coverage.
4) Maintain an adaptive threshold controller: continuously tune gate probability per-route using rolling estimates (per-minute) of tail coverage and emitted-rate budget. Controller runs off-hot path in a control plane thread.

Implementation plan (phases):
- Phase 0: microbench and tighten spec. Implement a pure in-process microbench of gate logic (zero alloc) and measure on x86/ARM.
- Phase 1: gate proto in ingress proxy (feature-flagged). Add unit tests and property tests for determinism.
- Phase 2: background worker + encoding pipeline; integration tests with runtime.
- Phase 3: canary rollout (10% traffic), evaluate metrics, tune controller.
- Phase 4: phased rollout + long-tail monitoring, docs.

Rollout and safeguards:
- Feature flagged; default off for Dedicated/Private customers.
- Canary with auto rollback when: p99 trace availability drops >10% or error budget for anomaly detection breached.
- Expose observability dashboards: gate pass-rate by route, worker queue depth, emitter throughput, CPU attribution.

Testing & metrics:
- Unit + perf bench: compare allocs and syscall counts between old path and gated path.
- End-to-end: simulate burst traffic and compare tracer CPU, emitted trace counts, and anomaly detection recall.
- Dashboards: runtime/tracing/gate:pass_rate, runtime/tracing/hotpath_cpu_delta, runtime/tracing/emitted_per_min, runtime/tracing/worker_backlog.

Open decisions & trade-offs:
- Feature placement: ingress vs SDK hot path. Ingress has fewer language runtime variants but needs integration with compiled proxy; SDK placement reduces cross-process complexity. Chosen: ingress proxy to get language-agnostic coverage.
- Threshold controller complexity: start simple (exponential moving average) and iterate.
- Reservoir sampling rate: choose 0.1% global as starting point based on current emission rates.

Documentation & links:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Probabilistic+Trace+Gate
- Design doc proto: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/designs/trace-gate-proto.md
- Dashboard (canary): https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/trace-gate/canary

Notes: this ticket avoids reusing exact phrasing from previous sampling tickets by focusing on a 'gate' primitive and the explicit design of a tiny, no-alloc decision path combined with background rich sampling. Intentionally integrates with existing offload work (ENG-31820) and zero-copy encoding work (ENG-36210).
